recommendation: Keep the core audit commit as-is. Any future changes to Permission scope or boundary wording should be made in HL7/data-access-policies, not by reintroducing or editing deleted core Permission source.
issue_request: FHIR-49908 was an Applied FHIR-core Change Request from the Security work group, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R6. It requested clearer Permission scope and boundary wording describing access-request context, rights to data under conditions, permit/deny behavior, residual obligations/filtering, examples, and the relationship to Consent and security labels.
initial_application: GitHub PR HL7/fhir#3405 listed FHIR-49908 and merged as d184c744863121ac3e8506c61633e10238e604f2. Its implementation commit 8866264bc8b086d26fb7c53ad0a71e2887e2ee9c changed source/permission/permission-introduction.xml with the requested scope and boundary language while Permission was active in source/fhir.ini.
additional_context: Later commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 removed source/permission, removed Permission from source/fhir.ini, hierarchy.xml, and resourcelist.html, and changed Security module links to the HL7 Data Access Policies IG. Current core source has no active Permission resource entry and source/secpriv-module.html links Permission to the external IG. The external HL7/data-access-policies source contains the FHIR-49908 wording in input/pagecontent/StructureDefinition-Permission-intro.xml.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit. No core source change was made because the Permission resource is outside the current core build scope and the applied wording is maintained in the external Data Access Policies IG.
